brief.conference_theme: Environmental and social regeneration: beyond sustainability
brief.panel_theme: Circularity at scale: regenerative sourcing and supply chains

plan.summary: Build a three-person panel on circularity at scale, focusing on regenerative sourcing and supply chains in business. Favor rising or established, budget-conscious candidates with prior conference or presentation experience, and balance sectors, career stages, places, and organization types; national reach allows searches beyond New Haven.
plan.location_focus: National; include New Haven and the Northeast where useful

angles: Business-school and supply-chain researchers studying circular procurement, regenerative agriculture, and scaling reuse
Researchers presenting at circular economy and sustainable business conferences
Corporate sourcing, procurement, and supply-chain leaders implementing circular or regenerative practices
Circular-economy consultants and nonprofit program leaders with practical case studies and conference presentations
State or federal circular-economy, sustainable materials, and responsible-sourcing policy specialists
Think-tank policy experts on producer responsibility and circular supply chains who present to business audiences
Founders of early-stage circular materials, reuse, and regenerative sourcing businesses with demonstrated scale-up work
Small and mid-sized company leaders presenting supply-chain circularity case studies at industry events
Nonprofit and coalition leaders advancing just, regenerative supply chains and circular sourcing
Community or worker-centered advocates connecting materials circularity with equitable sourcing, with public speaking experience
Business or sustainability reporters covering circular supply chains, regenerative sourcing, and materials innovation
Trade-publication editors or podcast hosts who moderate circular economy and sustainable business discussions

cards.name: Michele Sarazen
cards.job_title: Assistant Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering
cards.could_speak_on: How recovering and reusing carbon, metals, and minerals can extend circularity beyond plastics and support more regenerative supply chains.
talk_ideas: Closed-loop approaches to reclaiming carbon, metals, and minerals
Energy-efficient processes that enable circular material flows
Where circularity strategies encounter practical challenges
cards.bio: Michele Sarazen is an assistant professor of chemical and biological engineering at Princeton University and a co-organizer of the 2025 Andlinger Center annual meeting on circularity. She moderated a panel on innovative approaches in energy-efficient and sustainable processes that emphasize closed loops.
cards.why_fit: Her research and panel experience provide an academic perspective on the processes and materials recovery that can help circular supply chains scale.

past_speaking.event: Andlinger Center Annual Meeting: “Strategies for Circularity: Prospects and Challenges” — moderated the “New Frontiers in Circularity” panel

cards.fit_reason: Verified academic with directly relevant circularity expertise and documented experience moderating a circularity panel.

cards.name: Heather Liddell
cards.job_title: Presenter; Purdue University affiliation listed in conference agenda
cards.could_speak_on: Using material-efficiency assessment of U.S. manufacturing supply chains to identify where circularity can be scaled.
talk_ideas: Material-efficiency measurement across manufacturing supply chains
What supply-chain assessment reveals about circularity opportunities
Connecting systems analysis with business decisions on resource use
cards.bio: Heather Liddell presented research on a physically extended EEIO framework for material-efficiency assessment in U.S. manufacturing supply chains at the 2025 REMADE conference. The agenda lists Purdue as her affiliation and identifies her as a co-author with Purdue University researchers.
cards.why_fit: Her conference research directly examines material efficiency in manufacturing supply chains, a close match for a panel on circularity at scale.

past_speaking.event: REMADE Circular Economy Technology Summit & Conference

cards.fit_reason: Her verified research presentation directly addresses material efficiency in U.S. manufacturing supply chains.

cards.name: David Hinks
cards.could_speak_on: How textile circularity and material sourcing intersect with U.S. manufacturing and supply-chain resilience.
talk_ideas: Textile circularity and the future of U.S. manufacturing
Sourcing materials with circularity and resilience in view
Connecting textile innovation with business supply-chain decisions
cards.bio: David Hinks is listed as dean of NC State University’s Wilson College of Textiles. The 2025 REMADE conference agenda lists him as a keynote speaker on the future of American textiles.
cards.why_fit: His academic leadership in textiles and documented keynote at a circular-economy conference offer a sector-specific perspective on circular sourcing and supply chains.

past_speaking.event: REMADE Circular Economy Technology Summit & Conference — keynote address, “The Future of American Textiles: A Homeland Security Imperative”

cards.fit_reason: Verified textile-sector academic leader with a relevant conference keynote; brings a distinct supply-chain sector perspective.

cards.name: John Holm
cards.could_speak_on: How reverse logistics and reuse coalitions can help businesses scale circular sourcing and supply chains.
talk_ideas: Designing material reverse-logistics systems for circularity
Building coalitions to scale reuse economies
Lessons from circular logistics and city circularity strategy
cards.bio: John Holm is Senior Vice President at Pyxera Global, where he leads circular economy and climate strategy. His work includes material reverse logistics, city circularity strategy, and large-scale reuse-economy coalition-building.
credentials: 15+ years’ experience designing and executing circular-economy strategies
cards.why_fit: He brings hands-on experience with reverse logistics and reuse systems directly relevant to scaling regenerative sourcing and supply chains.

past_speaking.event: The Circular Supply Chain Coalition: Optimizing Circular Logistics (SPLC webinar)

notable_work: Circular logistics case study with FedEx and Pyxera Global, recognized with the 2025 SPLC Leadership Award for Circular Economy
cards.fit_reason: Strong practitioner match with directly relevant reverse-logistics and reuse experience, plus a verified public presentation.

cards.name: Deborah Dull
cards.could_speak_on: Practical levers for embedding circularity into supply-chain design, operations, and sourcing.
talk_ideas: Four actionable levers for circular supply chains
Scaling circularity through business operations
Turning supply-chain circularity concepts into implementation plans
cards.bio: Deborah Dull is the Founder of Circular Supply Chain Network. The Climate Week NYC event agenda identifies her as presenting a technical foundation on circular supply-chain levers.
cards.why_fit: Her network and focus on practical circular-supply-chain frameworks align closely with a business audience seeking actionable approaches to scaling circularity.
cards.fit_reason: Direct topic alignment and a scheduled technical-foundation presentation, though the listed summit date is in the future.

cards.name: Virginie Le Barbu
cards.could_speak_on: Corporate implementation lessons from Lenovo’s Circle 360 and regional circularity networks.
talk_ideas: Scaling circularity through corporate programs such as Circle 360
Connecting regional service, manufacturing, and reuse networks
Operational challenges in moving circularity from pilots to systems
cards.bio: Virginie Le Barbu is Executive Director, Global Sustainability at Lenovo. The Climate Week NYC agenda lists her presenting a Lenovo Circle 360 example of networked, regional circularity in operation.
cards.why_fit: She offers a corporate operating perspective on implementing circularity within a global technology company and supply network.
cards.fit_reason: Strong corporate implementation fit with a relevant scheduled case presentation; the event date is in the future.

cards.name: Mallory Anderson
cards.could_speak_on: How Minnesota’s packaging EPR law can shift producer responsibility and reshape the systems that supply, collect, and recover packaging.
talk_ideas: Putting packaging extended producer responsibility into practice
Producer fees and the economics of reuse, recycling, and composting
What businesses should prepare for in state packaging EPR programs
cards.bio: Mallory Anderson is a project manager at the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency. She has presented on Minnesota’s packaging extended producer responsibility law and discussed the program with an audience.
cards.why_fit: She brings a state implementation perspective directly relevant to producer accountability and circular packaging systems, and her prior presentations meet the brief’s preference for experienced speakers.

past_speaking.event: Project Optimist presentation on Minnesota’s Extended Producer Responsibility law

cards.fit_reason: Strong topical match with verified state agency role and two documented public speaking appearances.

cards.name: Kara Steward
cards.job_title: Recycling Market Development Center Coordinator, Solid Waste Management Program
cards.could_speak_on: How state market-development programs and public-private partnerships can expand demand for recycled feedstocks and make circular material flows viable at scale.
talk_ideas: Building domestic markets for recycled materials
Connecting recycled feedstocks with product and supply-chain demand
State policy and business collaboration for circular materials
cards.bio: Kara Steward is the Recycling Market Development Center Coordinator in the Solid Waste Management Program at the Washington State Department of Ecology. The center supports domestic markets for recyclable materials and works with businesses, public agencies, and other partners on circular materials initiatives.
cards.why_fit: She offers a government market-development perspective that complements producer responsibility by focusing on the demand, infrastructure, and partnerships needed to use recovered materials at scale.
cards.fit_reason: Good government-side fit on circular-material market development, with one verified conference speaking appearance.

cards.name: Nicole Portley
cards.job_title: Materials Management PRO Program Plan Lead
cards.could_speak_on: What state review and oversight of producer-responsibility plans can teach businesses about implementing circular packaging systems and meeting producer obligations.
talk_ideas: Reviewing producer responsibility organization plans
State oversight and producer accountability in packaging EPR
Implementation lessons from Oregon’s Recycling Modernization Act
cards.bio: Nicole Portley is the Materials Management PRO Program Plan Lead at the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality. She has represented DEQ in public discussion of the agency’s review and approval of a producer responsibility organization program plan under Oregon’s Recycling Modernization Act.
cards.why_fit: She brings a directly relevant state regulatory perspective on producer responsibility plan review and implementation, useful for a business audience navigating circular supply-chain requirements.

links.label: Oregon DEQ announcement on program-plan approval

cards.fit_reason: Highly relevant state policy and program-oversight expertise, with one verified conference speaking appearance.

cards.name: Alysia Garmulewicz
cards.could_speak_on: How businesses can scale circular and regenerative material sourcing through new materials and supply-chain practices.
talk_ideas: Scaling circular materials through business supply chains
Building commercial pathways for regenerative material sourcing
cards.bio: Alysia Garmulewicz is listed as Co-CEO and Founder of Materiom on the Circularity 25 speaker page. The page lists her among the event’s speakers.
cards.why_fit: Her founder role at a circular-materials organization aligns closely with the panel’s focus on sourcing and supply chains.
cards.fit_reason: Strong theme match through a founder role at a circular materials organization, plus a confirmed conference appearance.

cards.name: Adam Hill
cards.could_speak_on: How circular polymer solutions can be developed and scaled across business supply chains.
talk_ideas: Scaling circular polymer materials in supply chains
Commercial opportunities and barriers for circular plastics
cards.bio: Adam Hill is listed as Founder & CEO of Direct Polymers on the Circularity 25 speaker page. The page lists him among the event’s speakers.
cards.why_fit: His listed founder role at a polymers company offers an industry perspective relevant to scaling circular materials.
cards.fit_reason: Directly relevant founder role in polymers and a confirmed conference speaker appearance.

cards.name: Andy Ruben
cards.could_speak_on: What it takes to scale circular business models and embed reuse and resale into company supply chains.
talk_ideas: Scaling circular business models in retail
Integrating reuse and resale into supply-chain strategy
cards.bio: Andy Ruben is listed as Founder & Executive Chairman of Trove on the Circularity 25 speaker page. The page lists him among the event’s speakers.
cards.why_fit: His listed leadership role at a circular business makes him relevant to a business-focused discussion of scaling circularity.
cards.fit_reason: Relevant founder and executive perspective on circular business models, with a confirmed conference appearance.

cards.name: Adolfo Alzuphar
cards.could_speak_on: How farmer-led advocacy can help make regenerative sourcing and supply chains more equitable for the next generation of U.S. farmers.
talk_ideas: Building farmer-advocate networks to shape agricultural supply chains
Connecting agricultural equity with regenerative sourcing
What farmers need from buyers and policymakers to support resilient food systems
cards.bio: Adolfo Alzuphar is the Field Organizing Director at the National Young Farmers Coalition, where he leads efforts to resource and empower the next generation of farmers. He directs the Farmer-Advocate program, building networks of local leaders advancing agricultural equity and sustainability.
cards.why_fit: His farmer-led organizing perspective can bring community and equity considerations into a business-focused discussion of regenerative supply chains.
cards.fit_reason: Strong advocate fit with direct relevance to farmer networks and agricultural equity; the profile lists one speaking appearance, though it is for a future 2027 program.

cards.name: Catherine Weetman
cards.could_speak_on: How regenerative circular strategies can reshape sourcing and supply chains while creating value with fewer resources and less harm.
talk_ideas: Building circular and regenerative strategies into supply chains
Using circularity to create business value while reducing resource use
Lessons from circular-economy implementation across industries
cards.bio: Catherine Weetman is an author, speaker, and podcaster focused on circular and regenerative strategies. Her Rethink Global site describes her work helping organizations develop approaches that create value with fewer resources, less pollution, and less harm.
credentials: Author of A Circular Economy Handbook
cards.why_fit: Her circular-economy focus and business-facing communication experience offer a strong fit for a panel on scaling regenerative sourcing and supply chains. Her podcasting background may also support a moderator role.

past_speaking.event: Workshops and talks (listed on Rethink Global)

cards.fit_reason: Directly relevant circular and regenerative business expertise, with speaking and podcast credentials; the available page confirms the profile but gives limited detail on specific past appearances.
